index.title: React Core APIs and What's New in 19
index.lead: One page that walks you through the key combination of cross-layer Context passing and render performance, then catches up with React 19's new toys. Every demo ships with a render-count badge and usage code, so you can reproduce the conclusions yourself instead of memorizing the docs.

coreApis.useContext: Subscribe to and read a context

api.introTitle: The four APIs, broken down one by one
api.introDesc: Read how each one is used, then verify the conclusions yourself. The render counts in each demo come from RenderBadge (written into the DOM via ref + effect, so it never pollutes the render result).

purpose.createContext: Creates a data channel so components at any depth can read the same data without passing props down every layer.
purpose.useContext: Subscribes to the current value of a context. When it changes, every component reading it re-renders — no matter how deeply it is nested.
purpose.useMemo: Caches a computed result and reuses the previous value while dependencies stay unchanged — used to preserve references or skip expensive computations.
purpose.useCallback: Caches the function itself so that renders share the same reference, sparing memoized children from pointless re-renders.

points.createContext: defaultValue is easily mistaken for an initial value — it only applies when there is no Provider and is never modified by a child's setState.；It must be created at the module top level; written inside a component it produces a new Context on every render and forces consumers to remount.；Since React 19 you can use <Context value={...}> directly; <Context.Provider> is no longer mandatory.
points.useContext: Context changes pierce through memo: even memo-wrapped consumers re-render anyway.；So put fast-changing fields into their own Context to avoid re-rendering the whole tree over a single field.；A component reading useContext must also live inside the Provider subtree, otherwise it only gets the default value.
points.useMemo: useMemo is not a data cache but a reference guard: it recomputes as soon as dependencies change.；Cached references only pay off alongside memo or dependency comparison; otherwise the result is thrown away just the same.；Don't wrap everything in useMemo — when the computation is already cheap, the wrapper itself may cost more.
points.useCallback: useCallback(fn, deps) is equivalent to useMemo(() => fn, deps); the former is more expressive.；Outer variables used inside the callback must go into the dependency array, or you capture stale closure values.；The functional updater setX(prev => …) lets you keep the dependency array empty — the most common combination.

api.fallbackDefault: Falls back to the createContext default value
api.readInjected: Reads the value injected by the Provider
api.nestedNoProps: Below are three nested layers; the middle two receive no props at all:
api.stableCallback: Stable callback: the reference never changes, so the child doesn't re-render for nothing
api.inlineCallback: Inline callback: a brand-new function every render, so the memoized child must re-render
api.tickNote: Note that tick itself is never passed as a prop — it exists only to force the parent to re-render. That is exactly the value of useCallback: when the parent re-renders for unrelated reasons, memoized children shouldn't be dragged along.

context.introTitle: The four working together: theme color + todo list
context.introDesc: The tree below has three layers, and the middle one passes no props at all. Data flows down entirely through createContext + useContext; keeping components that shouldn't re-render from re-rendering relies on useMemo (caching the injected object and derived data) and useCallback (stable callback references). The render counter in each layer's top-right corner is the proof — click around and watch who re-renders.
context.statsFromContext: stats / theme both come from Context; this layer receives no props
context.layer2Title: Layer 2 · Layout container (wrapped in memo, consumes no Context)
context.layer2Hint: This layer neither receives nor forwards any data, and it is wrapped in memo, so context changes don't re-render it. Its children are genuine consumers though and still get woken directly — memo blocks props, not Context.
context.todoPlaceholder: Type a todo, then press Enter or click "Add"
context.layer3Hint: This layer keeps only the input text in useState; all business data comes from Context — that is the point of cross-layer passing: middle layers don't have to plumb the data.
context.observe1: Check / add a todo: LayerOne and LayerThree both re-render (the stats and todos they consume changed), while LayerTwo stays completely still.
context.observe2: Switch theme: every component consuming Context re-renders, including LayerThree which doesn't even use theme — because they all read the same value object. This is exactly why Context changes pierce through memo, and why high-frequency fields belong in their own Context.
context.observe3: Switch the filter: only consumers depending on filter / visible update, which shows how useMemo's dependency array decides when to recompute and when to reuse.

features.title: What's new in React 19
features.intro: Everything below comes from React 19.2, the version this project actually depends on; each card can be verified hands-on right in the browser.
features.realValue: Real value {n}: after clicking it shows +1 first, then about 800ms later it is overwritten by the real result (the button stays pending meanwhile)
features.namePlaceholder: Leave it blank or type a single character to see validation kick in
features.errShort: The name must be at least 2 characters
features.actionHint: No need to hand-write the onSubmit / useState / loading trio: action takes over submission, pending state and the result.
features.useHint: use(promise) suspends the current component, caught by the nearest Suspense boundary; the Promise must originate outside the component (otherwise every render creates a new one and it suspends forever).
features.idHint: The two instances each receive their own non-conflicting stable id (like :r1:), with label and input correctly associated — server rendering and client hydration agree.
features.filterPlaceholder: Type a number to filter 6000 rows
features.deferredPlaceholder: Type quickly and watch the gap between the two values
features.deferredStale: Rendering is falling behind the input…
features.deferredHint: How it differs from useTransition: that one declares the update non-urgent; this one deliberately degrades on read, suiting values that come from outside and are awkward to wrap in a transition.
features.syncHint: Toggle your system network switch and the status follows at once (driven by the browser's online / offline events)
features.effectHint: pushLog is defined with useEffectEvent: inside the effect it reads the latest logs without being listed as a dependency — room is the only dependency, so the connection is rebuilt only when the room changes.
features.refPlaceholder: ref is now just an ordinary prop
features.refHint: Function components can declare ref as an ordinary prop; React 19 no longer needs a forwardRef wrapper.

card.optDesc: Update the UI to the expected result first, then overwrite it with real data once the request returns; it rolls back automatically on failure.
card.actionDesc: One Hook gives you the submit result, the action to dispatch to the form, and the pending state, replacing the hand-written trio.
card.useTitle: Read a Promise inside a component
card.useDesc: Consume a Promise directly with use(), paired with Suspense for the loading state — the only Hook allowed to be called conditionally.
card.idDesc: Generates an id that stays consistent across server and client, designed for label↔input association, aria attributes and similar cases.
card.transitionDesc: Marks non-urgent state updates as interruptible: the input always keeps up while heavy list rendering yields.
card.deferredDesc: Declares that the value may stay stale for now, letting costly downstream rendering lag one step behind so typing always stays smooth.
card.syncDesc: Brings data outside React (browser APIs, third-party stores) safely into rendering — avoiding tearing.
card.effectTitle: Read the latest value in an effect
card.effectDesc: Lifts event logic out of the effect's dependencies: it reads the latest props/state without causing a re-subscription.
card.refTitle: ref is no longer a special prop
card.refDesc: Starting with React 19, function components can accept ref as an ordinary prop; forwardRef can retire.
